title: Provisioning: support partial stage re-run with cached artifacts (validation-only, perf-canary-only, etc.)
author: Gabe Wilson
release_notes: Operator-facing: provisioning runs can now re-run specific stages (ex: Validating only) without re-provisioning infra; cached artifacts are reused where safe and recorded in the audit trail.
description: Context: During the staging + customer pilots we repeatedly hit situations where a run failed late (Validating or perf-canary) and the only recovery path was to restart the entire provisioning workflow. That is slow and creates unnecessary churn (Terraform apply, node imaging/bootstrapping). This PR adds first-class support for partial stage re-run ("replay") from the operator CLI and the control-plane API, reusing cached artifacts produced by earlier stages when safe. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce stage attempt semantics for a single ProvisioningRun (a run can have multiple attempts per stage, sequentially). We persist attempt_number and link each stage execution to the artifacts it produced/consumed. (2) Add a partial re-run API: POST /v1/fleet/provisioning-runs/{run_id}:rerun with body { from_stage, stages?, reason }. Server validates allowed re-run (cannot skip required prerequisites unless artifacts exist and are still valid), emits structured events, and queues work starting at from_stage. (3) Add cached artifact reuse: Terraform outputs/state ref, rendered helm values + chart versions, cluster identity (kubeconfig secret ref), and perf-canary bundle ref are re-used if they are from the same run_id and still within TTL and the run is not marked "infra changed". We also invalidate caches automatically when inputs change (pool_config hash, image version, runtime chart version). (4) CLI: `rw fleet provision rerun --run <id> --from Validating` and `--stage PerfCanary` (alias), with `--dry-run` returning what will be reused vs re-executed. (5) Safety: introduce server-side guardrails so rerun cannot move a run to Ready unless all required gates have a successful attempt that matches the current config hash; fixes the most common operator footgun we saw in staging (rerun validation against a changed config). (6) Observability: new metrics for rerun_count and stage_attempts; structured event includes attempt_number and artifact_cache_hit/miss flags. Testing: unit tests for rerun eligibility + cache invalidation; integration tests for rerun-from-Validating and rerun-from-PerfCanary; failure injection asserts no duplicate resource creation and correct Ready gating. Notes: This builds on pause/resume + retry/backoff work in #48246 and #48241. Follow-up: UI affordance in Console for rerun (tracked in ENG-2763) and expanding artifact TTL policy by environment (staging vs prod).
commits: control-plane/provisioning: implement rerun eligibility + cache invalidation logic
api: POST provisioning-runs/:id:rerun endpoint + authz/audit trail
worker: queue stage executions from arbitrary stage w/ prerequisites enforcement
cli: add `provision rerun` command + dry-run output
tests: integration coverage for rerun-from-Validating and rerun-from-PerfCanary
metrics/events: add attempt_number + artifact_cache_hit labels (w/ cardinality guardrails)
conversation: Vanessa Ortiz (review): The operator story is solid. Two concerns: (1) can rerun accidentally reuse stale terraform outputs if the pool config changed? (2) do we record rerun reason in the audit log for later postmortems?

Gabe Wilson (author): Good call. Added `pool_config_hash` + `iac_module_version` into the artifact cache key and invalidate on mismatch. Also plumbed `reason` into `audit.provisioning.run.rerun_requested` and surfaced it in structured events.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please ensure rerun cannot transition to Ready without perf-canary success when perf-canary gate is enabled. We had a race bug earlier; want to be explicit here.

Gabe Wilson (author): Added `required_gates_satisfied()` check: it now verifies success attempts for Smoke, Validating, and PerfCanary (if enabled) *matching the current config hash* before setting Ready. Integration test added for the negative case.
Ethan Park (review): API shape: using `:rerun` suffix is fine, but please add rate limiting + admin-only guard. Also, can we return a "plan" in response so CLI can print cache hits?

Gabe Wilson (author): Added existing fleet-provisioning rate limiter bucket + `fleet.provisioning.rerun` permission (admin/operator). Response now returns `rerun_plan` summary (strings) for CLI; kept it low-cardinality.
Rina Kobayashi (review): Perf-canary artifact reuse: we should reuse the bundle ref, but not reuse results. Make sure perf-canary stage rerun forces a fresh execution.
Gabe Wilson (author): Yep. Cache reuse is only for the bundle ref + config; results are always a new attempt. The rerun plan explicitly says 'reuse bundle: yes, reuse results: no'.
Allison Grant (comment): Metrics labels: adding `artifact_cache_hit` is OK, but please keep it boolean and do not add per-artifact labels; we had a cardinality incident last quarter.
Gabe Wilson (author): Acknowledged. Implemented as a boolean per stage execution; no per-artifact labels. Added a test to ensure only the expected labels exist.
Vanessa Ortiz (approval): Looks good after changes; this will save us a ton of time during the pilot windows. Approved.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved. Please make sure runbook mentions rerun guardrails + how to read the rerun plan output.
Gabe Wilson (author): Added a short section to docs/internal/provisioning/cli.md; runbook update will be in Kira's doc PR.
